items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: Coltrane or Parker or Sonny Rollins are still on the list [of influences for young students]

ctx.x: Who are the great masters for 20-year-olds now? I mean we moved from generation to generation. You know Coltrane was the zenith for many years. Who do they cite now as their influences?

You know I mean it’s very interesting and that’s another great question. I mean we do ask a lot of the young students coming in to audition for us who apply to Michigan, you know who are you checking out and who are you interested in and you know almost to a fault there’ll be Coltrane or Parker or Sonny Rollins are still on the list. I mean I think that those players are still incredibly important to them. But there will be you know Patrick Bartley and you know, other younger players, and sometimes there are…

the masters. But also a body of younger players. And you know I don’t notice players so much — like Michael Brecker’s name may come up but it seems like there’s maybe a generation of players that are not getting listened to as much and maybe so we sort of stop in the early ‘60s and then they sort of missed some of the ‘60s, ‘70s and ‘80s, and then it’s more into the 2000s. So this is the first time I’m really thinking about it this way so it’s a half-formed thought but it does seem like the early masters are…
